blogs.title: Why Token‑Level Ratios Fail: The Hidden Instability in RL for Large Language Models
blogs.description: An accessible explanation of how traditional RL algorithms like GRPO use token‑level importance sampling, why this leads to high‑variance gradients and model collapse, and the core insight that the unit of optimization must match the unit of reward.

blogs.title: Introducing Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO): A Simpler, More Stable RL Algorithm
blogs.description: A walk‑through of the GSPO algorithm’s key ideas—sequence‑level importance ratios, length‑normalized clipping, and group‑based advantage estimation—showing how these changes solve the instability problems of GRPO.

blogs.title: Scaling Reinforcement Learning with Mixture‑of‑Experts Models: How GSPO Eliminates the Need for Routing Replay
blogs.description: Explains the specific challenges of training MoE language models with RL, what the Routing Replay technique does, and why GSPO’s sequence‑level approach naturally stabilizes MoE training without extra overhead.

blogs.title: From Theory to Practice: How GSPO Boosts Training Efficiency and Performance on Real Benchmarks
blogs.description: Summarizes the empirical results from the paper—reward curves, benchmark gains on AIME, CodeBench, and Codeforces—and illustrates why GSPO achieves higher sample efficiency despite clipping more tokens.

blogs.title: Bridging Training and Inference: Leveraging Sequence‑Level Likelihoods for Faster RL Pipelines
blogs.description: Discusses how GSPO’s reliance on whole‑sequence likelihoods reduces precision sensitivity, enabling direct use of inference‑engine scores, simplifying infrastructure for partial rollouts and multi‑turn reinforcement learning.
